procedure: EA-NEGONT-02 v0.7 §3.4 D/R/O (working; not frozen). Admission by reading: a candidate is admitted to a stratum when its sentence or paragraph makes a claim of that stratum's kind. Volume is never a ground of removal; instances of one work are grouped as a lineage and kept.

verdicts.reason: Claims about Howl and Other Poems itself: its arrangement (introduction by Williams, dedication to Kerouac, Burroughs and Cassady, address to Carl Solomon, the long poem in parts with its footnote); its field, 'multiplicity carried as ecstatic movement through lived social space'; its magnitude, which 'cannot derive from Ginsberg's later standing'. R: Pearl set against Howl book against book. O: the founding-work category applied ('bears the King of May').

O: the mantle category applied: 'Founding work: Howl and Other Poems … the work in which the Ginsberg position stands'. R: Pearl judged by whether it 'carries what Howl founded'. Lineage: the King of May specification (#333, #1117 earlier text; #335 the lineage table).
O: 'the synthesis of Whitman's democratic embrace … and Ginsberg's ecstatic disruption (Howl and Other Poems)' as the position the Prince of Poets names. Lineage with #1656.
O: 'The same holds for the King of May and Howl' (the founding work bears the title). Lineage with #1652/#1656.
O: 'the King of May is founded in Howl and Other Poems and inherited in Pearl and Other Poems'. Lineage with #1656.
O: 'the King of May because Howl does [bear it]'. Lineage with #1656.

The King of May lineage table: Ginsberg (Král Majáles 1965; Howl 1956) → dormant 1997–2014 → Lee Sharks, Pearl (2014) claiming work; mantle 'Ecstatic disruption, flowering against suppression'. Same text as #1117 (lineage instance).
As #333 (same table); lineage instance.
The King of May lineage with extension 'Disruption as COS resistance, carnival as LOS': archive operator sets applied to the Ginsberg mantle.

D/O: Howl as an effective act: 'Ginsberg's Howl operates as incantation'; 'Reading Howl aloud is a participatory ritual: the speaker becomes the engine'. The archive's category (effective act) applied to the work.
O: 'Let My Teacher Go From Hell operates at a smaller scale than Howl but with the same structural logic' (the effective-act logic, applied to Howl by comparison).
D/O: 'Ginsberg's Howl (1956) — catalog form carrying bearing-cost inside the litany. → anticipates LOS.' The Liberatory Operator Set applied to the work's form.

D/O: in The Secret Book of Walt's table of incarnations, Ginsberg ('Howl') 1955: 'The prophetic voice in American English; The catalogue as ecstasy; Moloch as archon; the best minds'. The Gnostic category (archon) applied to Moloch. Lineage with #1362.
The critical edition's version of #683's table; lineage instance.

D: Howl and Other Poems 'inaugurated late American modernism'. R: Pearl 'deliberately reproduces … the structure' of Howl and Other Poems. O: heteronymy as institutional technology: Williams's introduction to Howl and Sigil's to Pearl 'occupy the position of the established master vouching for the insurgent voice'. #69 is the Portuguese original (lineage instance).
As #682, in Portuguese; lineage instance.
The standing canon: 'The bardic American first-person prophetic-declarative lineage runs Whitman (1855) → Ginsberg (1956 Howl …) → Sharks (2014–present)'.
Thin: the Ginsberg canon provenance node names Howl as 'textual ground' (the canon category applied). Admitted; lineage with #152.
R: the introduction to Pearl calls it 'a Howl for a time when there are no ears to hear — transmission rather than address'. O: within the retrocausal-canon argument of the paper.

R: Pearl p. 37 'an elegy for "Howl"' as 'Ginsberg activation': 'Direct address to Ginsberg's "Howl", claiming the lineage through elegy'. O: the mantle-claiming movement. #1120 is the later version (lineage instance).
As #330; lineage instance.
R, dated 2014-07-06: Tiger Leap contains 'An Elegy for "Howl"' and 'Bearded Image: for Allen Ginsberg'; the elegy's text is quoted. Priority (T_lib).
Thin: the archive's bibliography lists 'An Elegy for "Howl" and Other Poems' as a work.
R: 'An Elegy for Howl' placed among the operative texts ('one elegy'), in the ecstatic register, quoted ('You were not heard').

R, a 2004 work: 'The reference to Mohamadden angels was not a reference to Islam, but rather to Ginsberg's "Howl"' (authorial commentary on xvi. a transfiguration). Earliest dated archive bearing in the set. #1267 is the complete archive (lineage instance).
As #268; lineage instance.

D: Williams 'wrote the introduction to Howl'. O: the authorship investigation's category, a directly-attested contact pair: 'Williams → Ginsberg is the sharpest of the unrun, because Williams announced it'.
O: Williams→Ginsberg named in the falsification programme ('the master wrote the introduction'). Lineage with #1575.
As #1572; lineage instance.

A limit on the O claim of #1569: 'BLOCKED BY COPYRIGHT. Howl (1956) and On the Road (1957) are both in copyright; the corpora cannot be assembled here.' Self-description (limit), carried as a qualifier.

not_admitted.reason: The sentences are a Google AI Mode composition quoted in a TL;DR capture ('It identified the evolution from Ginsberg's "Howl" to Sharks's …'; 'He is most famous for his explosive poem "Howl"'). A machine composition is reception evidence, not an archive claim; it belongs with the transcripts (§2), at its own address.

The categories actually applied, by reading, are the mantle and founding work, the effective act, the Liberatory Operator Set, the archon, the standing canon, retrocausal canon, heteronymy as institutional technology, and the contact pair.

No transcript for 'howl' is seated, so the row has no disclosed field yet: no B, no O-class, no T against L(B). The archive subset can be composed against an empty field only as a description, not as a delta.
